mainTopic: Chopping wood on יום טוב, and opening a sealed house or fastening on יום טוב (ביצה 31b)
overview: The גמרא first notices that the משנה seems to contradict itself: it says 'one may not chop at all' and then explains how to chop. שמואל answers that the משנה is missing words. Building beams and beams that broke on יום טוב may not be chopped, but a beam that broke before יום טוב may be chopped with a cleaver, and a ברייתא supports this. רב then rules on a two-sided tool: the narrow, cleaver-like side is allowed and the wide, ax-like side is forbidden. This ruling is reported in two versions. A new משנה follows: produce may be taken from a house through a hole that formed by itself, and רבי מאיר allows making the hole on purpose. The גמרא explains that the wall is loosely stacked bricks, and רבי זירא limits the permission to יום טוב, not שבת. Finally שמואל rules on rope fastenings on doors, and a ברייתא challenges him. He answers that it follows רבי מאיר, but another ברייתא says the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר here. The גמרא's reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say 'one may not chop at all' and then go on to describe how one may chop.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But didn't you say in the first part of the משנה that one may not chop at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the משנה. The beginning forbids chopping completely, but the end lists which tool to use for chopping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If chopping is totally forbidden, there is no reason to say which tools are allowed. The two parts of the משנה cannot both be read simply, so the גמרא needs a new way to read it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The first part of a משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
But didn't you say in the first part
phrases.notes: Literally 'you said.' The גמרא is talking to the משנה as if it were a person.

phrases.english: one may not chop at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A total ban on chopping cannot sit next to rules about how to chop.

steps.title: שמואל fills in the missing words of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the משנה is missing words. Beams from the construction pile, or a beam that broke on יום טוב, may not be chopped. A beam that broke before יום טוב may be chopped, but only with a cleaver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches. One may not chop from the pile of beams, nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב. But one may chop from a beam that broke before יום טוב. And when one chops, it may not be with an ax, a sickle or a saw, only with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל solves the contradiction by restoring words to the משנה. 'Not at all' refers only to certain beams, while the tool rules refer to a different, permitted beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban and the permission are now about two different cases. Building beams and beams that broke on יום טוב were not set aside for burning. A beam that broke before יום טוב was. Even for the permitted beam, a change is required: you must use a cleaver and not the usual weekday tools.

keyTerms.meaning: A pile (of beams stored for building)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'not at all' does not mean all chopping is forbidden. After שמואל's correction, it applies only to the construction pile and to a beam that broke on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The text is missing words
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין מִן הַסְּוָאר שֶׁל קוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: One may not chop from the pile of beams,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב.
But one may chop from a beam
that broke on the day before יום טוב.
And when they do chop it,
one may not chop with an ax,
nor with a sickle, nor with a saw,
only with a cleaver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restoring missing words to the text (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids all chopping and then also gives tool rules, which contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covers building beams and beams broken on יום טוב. A beam broken before יום טוב may be chopped, but only with a cleaver.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two separate issues for the rest of the סוגיא: which wood is allowed (מוכן) and which tool is allowed (a change from weekday chopping).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also forbids chopping from the building pile or from a beam that broke on יום טוב, because that wood was not prepared for use.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: One may not chop wood from the pile of beams, nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב, because it is not prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches שמואל's corrected version of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the same two forbidden cases and gives the reason: the wood is not מוכן (ready for use before יום טוב). This confirms that the ban in the משנה is about which wood may be used, not about chopping in general.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
Prepared, set aside for use before יום טוב

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One may not chop wood
neither from the pile of beams

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on יום טוב,
because it is not from what was prepared.

steps.raayaObject: שמואל's corrected reading of the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the same forbidden cases with the reason of מוכן
steps.whatToRemember: The ban is about the wood, not the act. Building beams and beams that broke on יום טוב are not מוכן. A beam that broke before יום טוב may be chopped, but with a cleaver.

steps.title: רב: only the wide side of the ax is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר שלמיא, quoting רב, says the ban on chopping with an ax applies only to its wide side. Chopping with its narrow side is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'not with an ax.' רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: This was taught only about its 'female' side. But with its 'male' side, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'not with an ax,' and רב narrows that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wide blade is the normal weekday way to chop, so it is forbidden. The narrow side is an unusual way to chop, so it counts as a change and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'female' side: the wide side of the ax
The 'male' side: the narrow side of the ax

phrases.english: 'And not with an ax.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only about its female side,
phrases.notes: This means the wide side of the blade, the side normally used for chopping.

phrases.english: but with its male side, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This means the narrow side of the ax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the question of which wood to the question of which tool, narrowing the ax rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the wide side of the ax is forbidden. Its narrow side is permitted.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the cleaver?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this. The משנה already allows a cleaver, and the narrow side of an ax works like a cleaver.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! We learned in the משנה that one may chop with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה already allows a cleaver, any narrow chopping edge should obviously be allowed too. So what new thing did רב teach?

phrases.english: It is obvious,
we learned 'with a cleaver'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 4 as unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling permitting the narrow side of the ax
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's permission for a cleaver already makes the narrow side of an ax obviously permitted.

steps.title: A tool with a forbidden side might seem forbidden on both sides
steps.stepSummary: Without רב's ruling, one might think a tool that is an ax on one side and a cleaver on the other is forbidden completely, since one side is forbidden. רב teaches that the cleaver side is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: This applies only to a plain cleaver. But a tool that is an ax and a cleaver together, I would say, since this side is forbidden, the other side is forbidden too. So רב teaches us that it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב's ruling is not obvious, because the ax is a tool with two different sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allowed a cleaver that is just a cleaver. With a combined tool, one might forbid both sides because they belong to one forbidden tool. רב teaches that we judge by the side actually used, so the narrow side is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (one part affects the other)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may chop a beam that broke before יום טוב only with a change from weekday chopping. A cleaver, or the narrow side of an ax, is allowed. The wide side of an ax is not.

phrases.english: You might have said:
This applies only to a cleaver by itself,
but for an ax and cleaver together, I would say:
phrases.notes: He means one tool that is an ax on one side and like a cleaver on the other.

phrases.english: since this side is forbidden,
this other side is also forbidden;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistake to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tool with one forbidden side is forbidden on both sides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each side is judged on its own, so the narrow cleaver-like side of an ax is permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Chopping on יום טוב with the narrow side of an ax is permitted, even though the wide side of the same tool is forbidden.

steps.title: Second version: רב's ruling is about the cleaver
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב's statement on the second part of the משנה, about the cleaver. A cleaver may be used only with its 'male' side. Using its 'female' side is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this ruling on the latter part of the משנה: 'rather, with a cleaver.' רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: the cleaver was allowed only with its male side. With its female side it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב's statement. Here it is attached to the משנה's words 'rather, with a cleaver' and limits how the cleaver may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 4), רב started from the ax and permitted its narrow side. In this version, רב starts from the cleaver and restricts it. Only the cleaver-like side is allowed, and the wide, ax-like side stays forbidden. The topic is the same, but the ruling now moves in the opposite direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (a second version of the same statement)
The latter clause of a משנה
The 'male' side of a tool, here the narrow cleaver edge
The 'female' side of a tool, here the wide ax-like side

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same ruling of רב, reported in a second way. In this version רב restricts the cleaver, while in the first version he permitted part of the ax.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the latter clause:
"Rather, with a cleaver."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only with its male side,
but with its female side, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Think of a tool with a narrow side and a wide side. The narrow side is allowed, and the wide side is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב's ruling from Step 4, attached to the cleaver clause instead of the ax clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cleaver is allowed on יום טוב only with its narrow (male) side. Its wide (female) side is forbidden.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious? The משנה already forbids an ax
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this. The משנה already says not to use an ax, and the wide side is just like an ax.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Didn't we learn in the משנה, 'not with an ax'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges this second version too. It says רב's ruling adds nothing, because the משנה already forbids an ax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wide side of the tool works like an ax. The משנה already bans an ax, so forbidding the wide side seems to repeat what we already know.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Didn't we learn "not with an ax"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version of רב's ruling as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the female (wide) side is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wide side is an ax, and the משנה already forbids an ax, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A two-sided tool might have been fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: Without רב, one might think a tool that is a cleaver on one side and an ax on the other is fully allowed, since one side is permitted. רב teaches that the ax side stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that applies only to a plain ax. But a tool that is both a cleaver and an ax, I would say: since this side is permitted, that side is permitted too. So רב teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's ruling was needed. It shows the mistaken conclusion a person might have reached without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids a plain ax. A combined tool is partly a permitted cleaver, so one might think the whole tool takes on that permitted status. רב teaches that each side keeps its own rule. This is the mirror image of Step 6, where one might have thought the whole tool was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken thought)
Since (one thing is true, the other should be too)
He teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רב's point is the same: on a two-sided tool, each side keeps its own rule. The cleaver side is allowed, and the ax side is forbidden.

phrases.english: You might have said: this applies only to an ax,
but a tool that is a cleaver and an ax, I would say:
since this side is permitted,
that side is also permitted;
so he teaches us that it is not.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a case the משנה did not clearly cover: a combined two-sided tool
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the cleaver side is permitted, the ax side of the same tool should be permitted too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ax side stays forbidden even when it is attached to a cleaver.

steps.title: New משנה: taking produce through a hole in a house
steps.stepSummary: If a house full of produce gets a hole in it, one may take produce out through that hole on יום טוב. רבי מאיר says one may even make a hole on purpose and take the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house that is full of produce and got a hole in it: one may take produce from the place of the hole. רבי מאיר says: one may even make a hole from the start and take produce.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses whether produce locked inside a house may be taken out through a hole on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows taking produce only through a hole that opened by itself. רבי מאיר goes further and allows a person to make the hole himself. The rest of the section asks how רבי מאיר can allow this.

keyTerms.meaning: Got a hole, was broken open

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A house that is full of produce, and a hole formed in it:
one may take produce from the place of the hole.
Rabbi Meir says:
One may even make a hole from the start and take produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce may be taken through a hole that formed by itself. רבי מאיר says one may even make the hole on purpose.

steps.title: Isn't making the hole tearing down a structure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר can allow making a hole. That seems to be tearing down a structure, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is this allowed? Isn't he tearing down a tent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's ruling. Breaking a hole in a wall looks like a forbidden act of demolition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking apart a structure is a forbidden מלאכה. Making a hole in a house's wall should count as that. So it is hard to see how רבי מאיר permits it, even to get food.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why is this allowed?
But he is tearing down a tent!
phrases.notes: 'Tent' here means any built structure. Here it is the wall of the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's permission to make a hole on purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a hole in a building is demolishing a structure, which is forbidden.

steps.title: The wall is just loosely stacked bricks
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the case is a wall of bricks stacked loosely without cement. That does not count as a real building.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי בר אדא said in the name of שמואל: the case is bricks stacked loosely on top of each other.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The 'wall' is just loose bricks, not a built structure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bricks that are only piled up, with no cement, are not a real building. Removing some of them is not considered tearing down. So רבי מאיר's ruling does not involve the forbidden act.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥumi bar Adda said that Shmuel said:
It is talking about loosely stacked bricks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hole is made in a real built wall, which would be tearing down.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hole is made in loose bricks, which are not a building.

steps.title: Challenge from רב נחמן: arranged bricks are set aside
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן said leftover bricks may be moved on שבת because people sit on them. But once they are arranged in rows, they are set aside and may not be moved. So even stacked bricks should be off-limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב נחמן said: bricks left over from a building may be moved on שבת, since they are fit to sit on. If he arranged them in a stack, he certainly set them aside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's answer. It quotes רב נחמן, who treats stacked bricks as set aside and not to be touched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loose leftover bricks are useful as seats, so they may be moved. Once someone stacks them neatly, he shows they are meant to stay in place. That makes them off-limits. So taking bricks from a stacked wall should still be forbidden, even without cement.

keyTerms.meaning: He set them aside (made them מוקצה)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Naḥman say:
these bricks that were left over from a building,
it is permitted to move them on Shabbat,
since they are fit to sit on.
If he arranged them in a stack,
he has certainly set them aside!
phrases.notes: Stacking them shows he no longer plans to use them as seats, so they may not be touched.

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that loose bricks may be taken apart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules that stacked bricks are set aside, so taking them from a stack should be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי מאיר spoke about יום טוב, not שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that רבי מאיר allowed this only on יום טוב. רב נחמן was talking about שבת, where it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: they said this about יום טוב, but not about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא settles the clash between שמואל and רב נחמן. He shows that each one is talking about a different day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's ruling says בשבתא, on שבת. רבי מאיר's permission applies only on יום טוב, where the rules here are more lenient. So both rulings stand, each for its own day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ, אֲבָל לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: They said this about a Festival, but not about Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by day: יום טוב versus שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר and רב נחמן are talking about the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר allows it on יום טוב. רב נחמן's ruling is about שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר's ruling and adds the same limit: it applies on יום טוב, not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught like this: רבי מאיר says, one may even make a hole from the start and take produce. They said this about יום טוב, but not about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי זירא said. This confirms his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats רבי מאיר's words from the משנה and openly adds 'on יום טוב, not on שבת'. So רבי זירא's distinction is not just his own idea. It is stated in an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר allows making a hole in a wall of loosely stacked bricks to get produce, but only on יום טוב. On שבת, stacked bricks are set aside and may not be taken.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Meir says:
One may even make a hole from the start and take produce.

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אָמְרוּ, אֲבָל לֹא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: They said this about a Festival, but not about Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's answer from Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that רבי מאיר's permission applies only on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי מאיר with the words 'on יום טוב, not on שבת'

steps.title: שמואל's rule on ground fastenings versus vessel fastenings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a fastening attached to the ground may only be untied. A fastening on a כלי may be untied, unraveled, or cut. The same rules apply on שבת and on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: With rope fastenings attached to the ground, you may untie the knot, but you may not unravel or cut the rope. With fastenings on vessels, you may untie, unravel, or cut. This is the same on שבת and on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about rope knots that hold doors closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something attached to the ground counts like a building, so unraveling or cutting its rope looks like tearing down a structure. Untying is fine because that is how the door is normally opened. Vessels are not buildings, so even cutting is allowed. שמואל gives no special leniency for יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Fastenings: knotted ropes that tie a door shut
The ground; here, something attached to the ground
Unravels the rope into its strands
Vessels or utensils, such as a cupboard

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'both שבת and יום טוב' is what sets up the challenge that follows.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Fastenings that are attached to the ground —
phrases.notes: Think of a rope knotted shut on the door of a pit or cellar dug into the ground.

phrases.aramaic: מַתִּיר, אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ.
phrases.english: one may untie, but not unravel and not cut.
Those on vessels —
one may untie, unravel, and cut,
both on Shabbat and on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of tearing down a structure, which was discussed with the brick wall, and applies it to door fastenings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ground fastenings may only be untied. Vessel fastenings may be untied, unraveled, or cut. No difference between שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows cutting ground fastenings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that ground fastenings may be unraveled and cut on יום טוב. This contradicts שמואל, who forbade it on both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: With fastenings attached to the ground, on שבת you may untie but not unravel or cut. On יום טוב you may untie, unravel, and cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל with a ברייתא that treats יום טוב more leniently than שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said ground fastenings may never be unraveled or cut, on either day. The ברייתא agrees about שבת but allows both on יום טוב. That directly clashes with שמואל's 'both שבת and יום טוב.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'They raised an objection': a challenge from a תנאי source

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Fastenings that are attached to the ground,
on Shabbat — one may untie
but not unravel and not cut.
On Yom Tov — one may untie, unravel, and cut!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that ground fastenings are treated the same on שבת and יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows unraveling and cutting ground fastenings on יום טוב, which שמואל forbids.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, but שמואל follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who allowed even making a hole in the brick wall. The רבנן disagree with him, and שמואל ruled like the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who said one may even make a hole from the start and take the fruit. The רבנן disagree with him, and I ruled like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends himself by saying the ברייתא reflects only רבי מאיר's lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר was lenient about breaking open a loose wall on יום טוב (Steps 10–15). So the ברייתא that allows cutting ground fastenings on יום טוב must be his. שמואל says he follows the stricter רבנן, who do not allow this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view is this?': used to assign a source to one particular opinion
From the start, as a first choice

phrases.english: Whose view is this —
it is Rabbi Meir, who said:
one may even make a hole from the start and take,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's ruling about breaking open the loose brick wall to take fruit, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis disagree with him,
and I spoke in accordance with the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: 'I' here is שמואל, explaining his own ruling.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a minority opinion that the ruling does not follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted הלכה and contradicts שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי מאיר's view only. שמואל follows the רבנן, who disagree.

steps.title: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about ground fastenings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's answer. A ברייתא says the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that ground fastenings may be unraveled and cut on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do the רבנן really disagree with him about ground fastenings? It was taught: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about ground fastenings, that on שבת one may untie but not unravel or cut, and on יום טוב one may untie, unravel, and cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down שמואל's answer by showing that the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר in this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's answer depended on the רבנן disagreeing with רבי מאיר. This ברייתא says that about fastenings, the חכמים agree with him. So, by this ברייתא, even the רבנן allow cutting on יום טוב, and שמואל's answer from Step 18 no longer works. The גמרא's reply comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is it so?': a question that doubts the previous claim
'But it was taught': introduces a ברייתא that contradicts a claim

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement between רבי מאיר and the רבנן was about breaking a wall. This ברייתא says that on fastenings, they agree.

phrases.english: But do the Rabbis disagree with him
about fastenings that are attached to the ground?
But it was taught: The Sages agree with Rabbi Meir
about fastenings that are attached to the ground,
that on Shabbat one may untie
— but not unravel and not cut,
on Yom Tov — one may untie, unravel, and cut!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ בְּחוֹתָמוֹת שֶׁבַּקַּרְקַע? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר about ground fastenings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא states that the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר here, so שמואל cannot be following the רבנן.
